messages:
sara_sales: Hey SE team — Riverbank asked if Redwood can act as a drop-in for their current vendor's API. They want a mapping doc + delta on pricing. Any immediate blockers?

bryan_se: quick summary from looking at their docs: param name mismatches (they use `max_tokens` vs our `max_new_tokens`), streaming chunk envelope is different, and their response wraps content in `choices[]` while our streaming uses `delta` messages. rate-limit headers different too.

bryan_se: they also rely on a function-calling flow where the model returns a `call` object. We have tool-calling that can match but need deterministic mapping rules.

matt_infra: For a POC we can provision a lightweight compatibility proxy that translates requests/responses. ETA ~2–3 days for a minimal shim + smoke tests. Need sample traffic + auth method (api key vs mTLS).

sara_sales: Prod asks: SOC2, SAML SSO, and VPC peering. For the POC they can accept a hosted test but legal wants the questionnaire filled. Any blockers to giving them a POC workspace?

elaine_sec: POC ok on hosted infra if data is test-only. We'll require signed NDA + completed security questionnaire before giving infra creds. Share the questionnaire here: https://redwood.internal/sec_qs/Riverbank.pdf

bryan_se: They sent a sample request, pasting minimal example they use: 
```json
{
  "model": "rival-3b",
  "prompt": "Summarize product requirements:\n- latency budget\n- edge cases",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "stop": ["\n\n" ]
}
```

bryan_se: Mapping notes: translate `max_tokens` -> `max_new_tokens`, keep `temperature`, and convert `stop` into our stop-sequence semantics. For streaming, proxy must rewrap our deltas into their `choices` chunks.

sara_sales: Pricing Q — they want to see per-token parity and a short analysis of cost delta if they move to Redwood Dedicated. How do we present that succinctly?

matt_infra: Provide two scenarios: hosted per-token estimate (using Optimize's recommended batching) and a Dedicated reservation scenario (monthly commit + lower unit cost). Include an example run of 1M tokens to show delta. I'll produce numbers after we run the smoke tests.

elaine_sec: Also flag legal: DPA + subprocessors must be approved. Ask them for cloud region and list of required retention policies. CC @legal.

ops-bot: Reminder: create POC workspace ticket #POC-872 assigned to bryan_se + sara_sales. Due date set to 2026-03-27.

bryan_se: Proposed POC checklist: 1) collect 200 sample prompts (dev/test/edge) 2) spin shim behind `/compat/v1` route 3) run 1k queries capture latency/outputs 4) diff outputs and log drift 5) iterate mapping rules and surface top 10 mismatches for customer review.

sara_sales: One more: stop-sequence behavior — do they need exact parity? This often trips up templates.

bryan_se: stop sequences usually match, but their runtime uses an `eos_token` heuristic that can truncate early on streaming. We'll document edgecases and add a compatibility flag `prefer_strict_stop: true` in the proxy for parity.

elaine_sec: I've started answering the security questionnaire; still need their list of subprocessors and retention answers. I'll attach our response PDF once complete.

sara_sales: Great — I'll gather samples and legal contact today, schedule kickoff Fri 11am. Thanks all :thumbsup:
